power_statement_top: A 1-2 pp/yr rotation edge cannot be shown by any test available to us. From 1998-2019 variance (full-tilt proxy, Holm m=3, 80% power) the minimum detectable effect is 2.6 pp/yr on pre-1998 plus 2020-2025 pooled, 9.2 pp/yr on 2020-2025 alone, 10.1 pp/yr after five forward years and 7.1 after ten. Detecting 2 pp/yr would need about 127 clean years; 1 pp/yr about 509. The historical tier is a low-power falsification screen, not a confirmation.

question: When conditions turn bad, does tilting from equal weight toward low-beta industries (defence) and back toward high-beta industries (offence) on a two-key signal add value over holding the same average mix, after costs?
prior_examination_disclosure: 1926-2019 has been examined for this question: v1 (market timing 1928-1997 on the French market; sector rules 1998-2019) and Pro run B (ten rules on French 49 industries 1926-2019, including R7 breadth divergence and R8 washout re-entry, near neighbours of H1, and R6 confluence-to-defensives, near twin of the H3 SI suggested). All negative. The pre-1998 window is therefore NOT clean and is not called clean; it is a falsification screen.

The lead saw some of run B's per-rule era rows (R5-R8, 1926-2019) while reading its file to record the trials. No v2 parameter or grid value was chosen from them; the grid below was set from SI's proposal and the arming check only.

construction.gap_rule_no_imputation: An industry enters a leg only after 252 valid daily returns. An industry-day with a missing return is dropped from that day's leg average and from that day's breadth, and is counted. No imputation, no substitute industry, no zero fill. Dropped industry-days are reported per window.
construction.legs: At each month-end t, beta of each eligible industry's daily returns to the French market (Mkt-RF+RF) over the 252 sessions ending t-1 (>= 200 valid pairs). OFFENCE = top third by beta, DEFENCE = bottom third (16 each with 49 industries; fewer before 1970), used for the following month. BASE = equal weight of all eligible industries, rebalanced monthly.

breadth_stand_ins.i: share of offence industries above their own 50-session SMA. Granularity 1/n_offence (about 1/16 = 6.25 pp); every grid threshold is a multiple of that step.
breadth_stand_ins.ii: narrowness: mean over offence industries of (equal-weighted minus value-weighted industry return over 60 sessions); continuous

construction.relative_line: cumulative offence-leg return over cumulative defence-leg return

H1.name: two-key switch vs the exposure-matched mix
H1.rule: States: NEUTRAL = base; DEFEND = defence leg; ATTACK = offence leg. ARMED when the relative line is within h% of its 126-session high AND offence breadth (i) is at least b pp below its own 126-session maximum. TRIGGERED when, while armed (or armed within the last 21 sessions), the relative line closes below its own 50-session SMA: switch to DEFEND. ATTACK after a washout-then-confirm: offence breadth (i) falls to <= 25% and then recovers to > 25% within 20 sessions. ATTACK and DEFEND revert to NEUTRAL at the next month-end unless re-triggered. Decision at close t, execution at close t+1; costs 10 bp per side on industry portfolios.

declared_grid.selection: the setting with the highest 1998-2019 annualised excess over its matched mix, chosen after freeze on 1998-2019 only; exact ties (difference below 1e-9) go to the more conservative setting: smaller h first, then larger b. All 4 settings are counted.

H1.arming_check_1998_2019: Armed fraction on breadth (i): 11.8% (h=3, b=25), 7.6% (3, 37.5), 19.7% (5, 25), 13.7% (5, 37.5); the price key alone is on 37% (h=3) / 50% (h=5). Not degenerate: breadth removes more than half of the price-key days, so H2 is not empty by construction. Stand-in (ii) armed fraction (bottom 20% of its 6-month range) is 6.9% / 9.8%; it is recorded and not used, because (i) is not degenerate. No return was computed (v2_power/arming_check_D.py).
H1.primary_contrast: annualised mean daily return of H1 minus the exposure-matched static mix of offence, defence and base at H1's average weights, rebuilt inside every bootstrap resample from that resample's own average weights (parent ruling A)
H1.differs_from_run_B_R7: R7 is prior negative evidence against H1's breadth key. H1 differs in two ways: (1) a second key is required - the offence/defence relative line must break its 50-session SMA after arming; R7 switched on the breadth drop alone; (2) legs are beta-sorted thirds re-formed monthly from data to t-1, not R7's fixed named cyclical and defensive groups; H1 also starts from equal weight, not from the cyclical leg.

precedence.defend_and_attack_same_day: If the DEFEND trigger and the ATTACK confirmation are both true at the same close, DEFEND wins (the defensive state is taken; the attack confirmation is discarded and the washout flag is reset).
precedence.trigger_on_last_session_of_month: A trigger or confirmation at the last session of a month executes at the next close and is held to the end of the FOLLOWING month; the month-end reversion to NEUTRAL applies only to states set before the month's last session. Legs re-formed at that month-end are the legs the new state holds.
precedence.precedence_with_neutral: A state already in force and re-triggered on a later day is extended to the end of the month of the re-trigger (same rule as above).

H2.name: breadth adds information
H2.rule: H1 minus the identical rule with the breadth key removed (armed = relative line within h% of its 126-session high alone; same h as selected for H1; same trigger and attack rules). Paired daily difference.
H2.primary_contrast: annualised mean of the paired daily difference H1 - H1_price_only
H2.inherits: H2's price-only control and the cash ablation use exactly the H1 grid point selected on 1998-2019; no second selection is made for any derived book.

H3.name: simplest direct control: 126-day relative momentum between the legs (run B R5 on beta-sorted legs)
H3.rule: At each month-end hold the offence leg if its 126-session return exceeds the defence leg's, else the defence leg. No parameters beyond 126.
H3.primary_contrast: vs its exposure-matched static mix, rebuilt inside each resample
H3.why: Parent ruling 12:05Z; trend-and-Sahm with defensives (SI's suggestion) is run B R6's near twin and showed no benefit. I have no better-motivated candidate.

hypotheses.mandatory_ablation: H1 with cash in place of the defence leg (identical DEFEND dates, bills instead of defensives); reported, not tested Inherits H1's selected grid point; no second selection.

power.method: 1998-2019 variance only; full-tilt proxy (switch between the beta-sorted legs on the price-only key minus its matched mix, matched mix rebuilt per resample); no mean or point estimate printed; v2_power/power_v2_D.py and .stdout
power.run_C_arithmetic: about 6 pp/yr detectable at five forward years with 5% active volatility; worse at higher volatility; adopted.
power.plain: H1's tilt is at most the full-tilt proxy, so its active risk is lower and the true numbers are between these and somewhat smaller; the conclusion does not change: a 1-2 pp/yr edge is not demonstrable historically or in five forward years.

pass_probability_under_joint_rule.method: normal approximation; per-window SE = D per-year sd / sqrt(years); windows 1928-45 (17.2y), 1946-97 (52y), 2020-25 (6y) treated as independent; D variance only, no point estimate
pass_probability_under_joint_rule.plain: The four positive-sign requirements cut the chance of passing at the MDE from 80% to about 63% (the 2020-2025 sign alone costs most of it), before the drawdown and 2x-cost conditions, which cut it further. A fail of this test is therefore NOT evidence of no effect: at a true 2 pp/yr edge it fails more often than it passes.
